1.1: There was this man named Job, livin' in the land of Uz. Real solid dude—blameless, straight-up, feared God, and stayed far from evil.
1.2: He had seven sons and three daughters.
1.3: Bruh was loaded. He owned seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred pairs of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and had mad workers. He was that guy out East—nobody had it like Job.
1.4: His sons used to throw feasts on their own scheduled days, and they'd invite their three sisters to come eat and drink with 'em.
1.5: After the party days wrapped up, Job would get up early, pray over his kids, and offer burnt sacrifices for all of 'em. He was like, 'Just in case one of them messed up or disrespected God in their hearts.' He did that every time—dude was committed.
1.6: One day, the heavenly crew came to check in with the Lord, and Satan slid in too.
1.7: The Lord said, 'Where you been?' Satan said, 'You know me—I've been out here roaming, walkin' all over the earth.'
1.8: Then God hit him with, 'So you peeped my guy Job, huh? Ain't nobody like him—solid, upright, fears Me, and don't mess with evil.'
1.9: Satan said, 'But Job ain't just loyal for nothin', though.'
1.10: 'You done put a whole fence around him, his family, and everything he own. He blessed because You blessed him. His bag is up cause of You.'
1.11: 'But let You touch his stuff, take it all away—watch him curse You to Your face.'
1.12: God said, 'Bet. You can do what you want with everything he got, just don't lay a hand on him.' So Satan dipped out from God's presence.
1.13: One day, Job's kids was all chillin', eatin' and drinking at the oldest brother's house.
1.14: Then a messenger came runnin' to Job like, 'The oxen were out workin' the field, and the donkeys nearby,'
1.15: 'When the Sabeans rolled up, took all the animals, and killed the workers. I'm the only one who made it out to tell you!'
1.16: While he was still talkin', another one pulled up: 'Fire from the sky—God's fire—came down and burned up the sheep and all the servants. I'm the only one who got out to tell you!'
1.17: Before he could finish, another dude ran in: 'The Chaldeans came in three squads, jacked all your camels, and killed the crew. I'm the only one left to tell you!'
1.18: And while he was still talkin', another burst in: 'Your sons and daughters were eatin' and drinkin' at the oldest brother's place,'
1.19: 'When a wild wind came outta nowhere, hit all four corners of the house—it collapsed. Everybody gone. I'm the only one who survived to tell you.'
1.20: Then Job stood up, tore his robe, shaved his head, fell to the ground—and worshipped.
1.21: He said, 'I came in this world with nothin', and I'ma leave with nothin'. The Lord gave it, the Lord took it away. Blessed be the name of the Lord.'
1.22: Through all this? Job ain't sin. He didn't blame God for anything.

2.1: Another day came around when God's heavenly crew pulled up to check in, and guess who showed up again? Yep—Satan was right there in the mix.
2.2: The Lord said to him, 'Where you been?' Satan said, 'Just out here, you know—roamin' the earth, walkin' around, peepin' everything.'
2.3: Then God said, 'So what about my guy Job? Still holdin' it down. Ain't nobody like him—blameless, real one, fears Me, stays away from evil. And even after you had Me let you mess with him for no reason, he still ain't switch up. Still solid.'
2.4: Satan said, 'Man, skin for skin! A man'll give up anything to save his own life.'
2.5: 'But go ahead—touch his body, his bones, his flesh. Bet he'll curse You to Your face.'
2.6: God said, 'Alright then—he's in your hands. Just don't kill him.'
2.7: So Satan dipped out and hit Job with nasty, painful boils—head to toe, feet to scalp.
2.8: Job ended up sittin' in ashes, scratchin' himself with a broken piece of pottery. That's all he had left.
2.9: Then his wife said, 'You still tryna keep your integrity? Just curse God and die already.'
2.10: Job said, 'Girl, you soundin' real foolish right now. Should we only take the good from God but not the bad too?' And even with all that pain, Job ain't say one sinful word.
2.11: When Job's three boys—Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuh, and Zophar from Naamah—heard about everything that happened, they pulled up from their own cities. They planned it out ahead of time to come sit with him, mourn with him, and try to comfort him.
2.12: When they got close and saw him from a distance, they didn't even recognize him. They broke down cryin', tore their robes, and threw dust in the air over their heads.
2.13: Then they just sat with him on the ground for seven days and seven nights. Didn't say a single word—'cause they could see the pain on him was too deep.

3.1: After all that, Job finally opened his mouth and cursed the day he was born.
3.3: 'Forget the day I came into this world, And the night somebody said, "It's a boy!"'
3.4: 'Let that day be straight-up darkness. Don't let God even look for it. Let the sun skip over it like it don't exist.'
3.5: 'Let darkness and death take claim on that day. Let a thick cloud smother it. Let it be shook by the terror of gloom.'
3.6: 'And that night? Let it get snatched by the shadows. Don't let it celebrate with the rest of the year. Leave it out the calendar like it never mattered.'
3.7: 'Let that night be dry—empty. No joy, no shouts, nothin'.'
3.8: 'Let the ones who curse days go in on it— The same folks who wake Leviathan up.'
3.9: 'Let its morning stars go dark. Let it hope for sunrise and get none. Let the daylight skip it like it's cursed.'
3.10: 'All 'cause it ain't block me from being born. It didn't keep me from all this pain I see now.'
3.11: 'Why didn't I just die when I was born? Why didn't I go out as soon as I came out the womb?'
3.12: 'Why was I even laid on somebody's knees? Why did they nurse me like I was supposed to grow up?'
3.13: 'If I had died, I'd be quiet by now. Sleepin'. At peace.'
3.14: 'I'd be laid out with kings and big-time leaders, The ones who built monuments that now sit in ruins.'
3.15: 'Or maybe with princes who stashed gold, And had silver piled up in their houses.'
3.16: 'Or maybe I should've been like a miscarriage, Like a baby who never saw the light of day.'
3.17: 'Where I'd be, the wicked ain't start nothin'. And the tired folks finally rest.'
3.18: 'Even the prisoners chill together. They don't hear no more yelling from oppressors.'
3.19: 'Everybody there—big or small. And the servant ain't got no boss no more.'
3.20: 'So why is light even given to people goin' through it? Why keep breathin' when your soul is bitter?'
3.21: 'Folks out here beggin' for death, Lookin' for it like it's treasure buried in the ground.'
3.22: 'And when they finally find a grave? They get hype, like they won the lottery.'
3.23: 'Why give life to somebody who can't see a way out? Somebody God done boxed in on every side?'
3.24: 'I'm cryin' before I can even eat. Groans be pourin' outta me like water.'
3.25: 'The thing I feared the most? It happened. The nightmare I tried to dodge? It pulled up on me.'
3.26: 'I ain't got no peace, no quiet, no break. Just pain—back to back to back.'

4.1: Then Eliphaz from Teman spoke up and said,
4.2: 'Bruh, if I say somethin', you gon' get mad? 'Cause honestly, I can't just sit here quiet.'
4.3: 'You the one who used to teach folks, Liftin' up the ones who was weak and worn down.'
4.4: 'Your words used to hold up folks who was about to fall, And you gave strength to shaky knees.'
4.5: 'But now that it's hittin' you? You out here overwhelmed and broken.'
4.6: 'Wasn't it your fear of God that gave you confidence? Wasn't it your integrity that kept you grounded?'
4.7: 'Let's think—who ever died for no reason, bein' innocent? When did the good folks ever get wiped out for nothin'?'
4.8: 'From what I've seen, If you plant mess, you gon' grow mess. If you spread drama, it's gon' come back around.'
4.9: 'God's breath alone can take folks out. His anger is like fire—it consumes.'
4.10: 'Lions may roar all tough, Young lions might show their teeth, But all of 'em can get their power snatched in a second.'
4.11: 'Old lions die if they can't find food. And the cubs? Scattered with no protection.'
4.12: 'Now let me tell you somethin' I heard on the low. It came to me in a whisper.'
4.13: 'In one of them eerie night visions— You know, when folks fall into deep sleep?'
4.14: 'A chill hit me. I started shakin'. My bones? Felt like they was about to crack.'
4.15: 'Then somethin'—a spirit—passed by my face. The hair on my body stood straight up.'
4.16: 'It stopped, but I couldn't make out what it was. There was this shadowy form, and silence. Then a voice broke through:'
4.17: "'Can a human be more righteous than God? Can anybody be purer than the One who made 'em?'"
4.18: "'If He don't even fully trust His own servants, And He's called out His angels when they slipped…'"
4.19: "'…Then how much more us—just dirt and bones, Livin' in bodies made of clay, easy to crush like bugs?'"
4.20: "'From sun-up to sundown, folks fall apart. They die off, and nobody even notices.'"
4.21: "'Even the strong ones fade. They die with no wisdom, no legacy.'"

5.1: 'Go 'head and cry out. See if anybody gon' answer. Which one of God's holy ones you think gon' pull up for you?'
5.2: 'Anger kills the fool, And jealousy? That'll take out the simple-minded quick.'
5.3: 'I seen fools settlin' down, tryna build somethin'. Next thing I know—I was speakin' curses over their whole house.'
5.4: 'Their kids? Nowhere near safe. They get crushed at the city gates, and nobody showin' up to save 'em.'
5.5: 'Hungry folks come and eat up everything they worked for, Even grabbin' from the thorns. Traps snatch up what they got left.'
5.6: 'Pain don't just pop up from nowhere, And trouble don't grow like crops from the ground.'
5.7: 'But humans? We born into drama, Just like sparks naturally fly up off a fire.'
5.8: 'If it was me? I'd be seekin' God, I'd be takin' all my mess to Him.'
5.9: 'God do big things—wild, unsearchable stuff. Miracles that don't even have a number.'
5.10: 'He sends rain on the land, Waters the fields like clockwork.'
5.11: 'He lifts up the humble, And gives safety to those who mournin'.'
5.12: 'He messes up the plans of the slick ones, So their schemes fall flat.'
5.13: 'He traps the "wise" in their own game. They trip over the same tricks they set for others.'
5.14: 'They end up feelin' around in broad daylight like it's midnight. Can't see nothin', can't do nothin'.'
5.15: 'But God steps in and saves the broke and beaten, Rescues them from powerful mouths and greedy hands.'
5.16: 'So now the poor got somethin' to hope in, And injustice gotta shut her mouth.'
5.17: 'Look, the one God corrects? That man blessed. So don't get mad when the Almighty check you.'
5.18: 'Yeah, He might bruise you, But He also wraps you up and heals. He might wound, but His hands can make you whole again.'
5.19: 'He gon' bring you outta six struggles, And if a seventh one hit? Evil still won't touch you.'
5.20: 'If famine hit? He'll keep you alive. If war break out? You safe from the sword.'
5.21: 'When folks talk bad on your name, you covered. You won't be shook when destruction come knockin'.'
5.22: 'You'll laugh at chaos and hunger, And wild animals? You won't be scared of them either.'
5.23: 'You'll be so locked in with the land, Even the rocks won't trip you up. And the animals? They'll be at peace with you too.'
5.24: 'You'll know your home's at peace, And when you check up on your people, everything's in place.'
5.25: 'Your family? It's gon' multiply. Your kids? Spread out like grass in the field.'
5.26: 'You gon' leave this earth full of years, Like wheat harvested at the perfect time.'
5.27: 'Look, we ain't just talkin'. We done looked into this ourselves. It's real. So listen close—and take it in for yourself.'

6.1: Then Job spoke up and said,
6.2: 'Man... if only my pain could be weighed out, And my suffering thrown on the scale next to it.'
6.3: 'It'd be heavier than all the sand on the beach— That's why I been talkin' reckless.'
6.4: 'God shot arrows in me, and they deep. My spirit drinkin' poison, And His terrors? They lined up all around me.'
6.5: 'A wild donkey don't cry out if it got grass. An ox don't moan if it got food.'
6.6: 'Who eats bland food without salt? Ain't nobody tryna eat egg whites with no flavor.'
6.7: 'My soul rejects that mess— It's disgusting, like food that make you gag.'
6.8: 'I wish God would just hear me out And give me what I'm beggin' for.'
6.9: 'That He'd be willing to end it, Just let go and cut me off.'
6.10: 'Even in that, I'd find some kind of peace. I'd shout through the pain, 'Cause at least I ain't been quiet about what God said.'
6.11: 'What strength I got left to hold onto hope? What future am I even hangin' on for?'
6.12: 'I ain't made of stone. My body ain't bronze.'
6.13: 'Do I look like I got help in me? My strength done dried up, success gone.'
6.14: 'When somebody's down bad, their people supposed to show love— Even if that person ain't perfect or spiritual at the moment.'
6.15: 'But my boys? Y'all switched up on me. Like a creek that runs deep one day, Then dries up without warning.'
6.16: 'Y'all all cold and icy on the surface, But the snow melts and y'all disappear.'
6.17: 'When things heat up, y'all vanish. Can't count on y'all when it's real.'
6.18: 'Y'all paths lead nowhere. No help, no direction—just fade out.'
6.19: 'Caravans from Tema waitin' on y'all, Folks from Sheba lookin' for help.'
6.20: 'They showed up expectin' somethin'— And left confused and disappointed.'
6.21: 'Just like y'all. Now that I'm in pain, y'all scared and pulled away.'
6.22: 'Did I ask y'all for anything? Did I beg for your money or help?'
6.23: 'Did I say, "Rescue me from my enemies?" "Buy me out from the ones oppressin' me?" Nah.'
6.24: 'If I'm wrong, teach me. I'll shut up. Just help me understand what I did.'
6.25: 'Good words hit hard, But y'all arguments? They ain't proved nothin'.'
6.26: 'You tryna check my words? Man, I'm speakin' from pain—these cries just wind.'
6.27: 'You beat down orphans, And betray your friends in the process.'
6.28: 'Come on, look me in the eyes. I ain't never lied to your face.'
6.29: 'Chill out—don't bring injustice into this. I'm still standin' on my righteousness.'
6.30: 'Ain't no crookedness in what I'm sayin'. My spirit can tell when somethin' ain't right.'

7.1: "Ain't life on earth like hard labor? Ain't a man's days like a temp worker's grind?"
7.2: "Like a servant beggin' for shade, Like a day laborer waitin' to get paid—"
7.3: "That's how I've been livin'. Months of nothin'. Long, miserable nights I didn't ask for."
7.4: "When I lay down, I be like, 'How long 'til morning?' I toss and turn all night—ain't no peace till sunrise."
7.5: "My skin? Covered in worms and dirt. It's cracked, breakin' open again and again."
7.6: "My days fly by faster than a weaver's needle, And still, I ain't got no hope."
7.7: "God, remember—my life is just a breath. I'll never see anything good again."
7.8: "People who see me now? Won't see me no more. You'll look for me, but I'll be gone."
7.9: "Just like clouds disappear and fade, When somebody go to the grave, they don't come back."
7.10: "They don't come home. Their place don't even recognize 'em no more."
7.11: "So nah, I ain't holdin' my tongue. I'm speakin' from my pain. I'm hurt, and I got every right to complain."
7.12: "What am I—some sea monster? Why You got me locked down like I'm dangerous?"
7.13: "I tell myself, 'At least my bed will comfort me, My couch will ease this pain.'"
7.14: "But even in sleep, You haunt me with nightmares, Hit me with visions that shake me to my core."
7.15: "It's so bad I'd rather choke, I'd rather die than keep livin' in this body."
7.16: "I hate my life. I don't want forever—I just want peace. Leave me alone. My days short anyway."
7.17: "Why You even care about humans like this? Why we matter so much to You?"
7.18: "You check on us every morning, And test us every second of the day."
7.19: "How long You gon' stay on me? Can't I even catch a breath without You watchin'?"
7.20: "Did I sin? What did I do to You, God? Why You got me as Your target, Till I can't even stand myself?"
7.21: "Why not just forgive me? Wipe away my mistakes? 'Cause I'm about to lay down in the dirt— You might look for me, but I'll be gone."

8.1: Then Bildad the Shuhite jumped in and said,
8.2: 'How long you gon' keep talkin' like this, Job? You sound like a storm—just wind blowin' everywhere.'
8.3: 'You think God messes up justice? You think the Almighty get it wrong on judgment?'
8.4: 'If your sons sinned against Him, Then He let 'em face the consequences. That's on them.'
8.5: 'But if you'd just really seek God, Cry out to the Almighty for real—'
8.6: 'If you pure and upright like you say, Then by now He'd already be movin' for you. He'd bless your home again.'
8.7: 'Even if you started out small, Your ending would be overflowing with abundance.'
8.8: 'Look—ask the old heads. Check what our ancestors passed down.'
8.9: 'We just got here. We don't know nothin' yet. Our days on earth? Like shadows—blink and they gone.'
8.10: 'Won't they teach you somethin'? Won't they speak real wisdom from deep in their hearts?'
8.11: 'Can papyrus grow without swamp water? Can reeds pop up without moisture?'
8.12: 'They look strong while they green, But they wither faster than anything else once the water's gone.'
8.13: 'That's how it is for anybody who forgets God. The hope of fake folks gon' die out quick.'
8.14: 'They lean on weak stuff like spider webs— It snaps the moment they try to rest on it.'
8.15: 'He trust his house, but it collapses. He hold on tight, but it don't last.'
8.16: 'He might look fresh in the sunlight, His garden stretchin' out with pride.'
8.17: 'His roots twist through the rocks, Searchin' for somethin' solid to grip.'
8.18: 'But let him get snatched from his spot— Even the ground gon' act brand new, like, "I don't know him."'
8.19: 'That's the end of that man's joy. But somebody else gon' rise up out that same dirt.'
8.20: 'Look, God don't throw away the righteous, And He ain't out here co-signing evil.'
8.21: 'He'll fill your mouth with laughter again, And your lips gon' shout with joy.'
8.22: 'The ones who hated on you? They gon' be embarrassed. The place where wicked folks lived? Gone like it was never there.'

9.2: 'Yeah, I know what y'all sayin' is true— But for real, how can anybody be right in front of God?'
9.3: 'If somebody tried to argue with Him, They couldn't get one word right outta a thousand.'
9.4: 'God got wisdom for days and strength unmatched. Ain't nobody gone toe-to-toe with Him and came out winning.'
9.5: 'He moves mountains, and they don't even see it comin'. He flips 'em over when He's mad.'
9.6: 'He shakes the whole earth outta place— Even the foundations tremble.'
9.7: 'He tells the sun not to shine, and it listens. He shuts down the stars like they on a switch.'
9.8: 'He by Himself stretched out the heavens, And He walkin' on top of ocean waves like it's pavement.'
9.9: 'He made the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, And all them star clusters in the southern skies.'
9.10: 'He do things too wild for us to figure out— Wonders we couldn't count even if we tried.'
9.11: 'He could walk right past me and I wouldn't even know it. Slide by me and I'd never see Him.'
9.12: 'If He takes somethin', who gon' stop Him? Who got the nerve to ask, "Yo, what You doin'?"'
9.13: 'When God's angry, He don't back down. Even the proud folks get laid out in front of Him.'
9.14: 'So how I'm supposed to answer Him? What words I got that could stand up to God?'
9.15: 'Even if I was righteous, I couldn't argue. I'd just be beggin' Him for mercy.'
9.16: 'If I called and He picked up? I still wouldn't believe He really listenin' to me.'
9.17: 'He hit me with storms, Keeps stackin' wounds on top of wounds for no reason.'
9.18: 'He don't even let me breathe— Just fills me up with bitterness.'
9.19: 'If it's about strength—He got it. If it's about justice—who out here settin' the court date?'
9.20: 'Even if I was right, my own mouth would take me down. Even if I was innocent, my words would still make me sound guilty.'
9.21: 'I know I didn't do nothin', but I don't even recognize myself no more. I'm sick of life.'
9.22: 'It don't even matter. God destroys both the good and the wicked.'
9.23: 'If a disaster hits quick, He sittin' back laughin' at the innocent goin' through it.'
9.24: 'Seems like the world done been handed to the wicked. Even the judges can't see straight—like He got 'em blindfolded. And if it ain't Him doin' it… who else could it be?'
9.25: 'My days movin' faster than a sprinter— They run past and I don't see a lick of good.'
9.26: 'They gone like fast ships on the water, Or like an eagle divebombin' on its prey.'
9.27: 'If I try to fake it—say I'm good, Put on a smile and hide the pain—'
9.28: 'I still stay shook from all this suffering. I know You ain't about to clear me.'
9.29: 'So if I'm already guilty in Your eyes, Why I'm even tryin'? What's the point?'
9.30: 'Even if I scrubbed myself with snow water, And used all the soap in the world—'
9.31: 'You'd still toss me in the dirt, And even my clothes would be disgusted with me.'
9.32: 'God ain't human like me, So I can't just argue back or take Him to court.'
9.33: 'Ain't nobody in the middle to mediate this— Nobody to lay hands on both sides and bring peace.'
9.34: 'If He'd just take His rod off me, And stop terrifying me with His presence—'
9.35: 'Then maybe I could speak up without fear. But right now? That ain't my reality.'

10.1: Man, I'm sick of life. I'ma let my complaints fly free, Speak straight from the bitterness in my soul.
10.2: 'God, don't just write me off. Tell me what I did wrong. Why You comin' for me like this?'
10.3: 'Do You really get joy outta crushin' me? Dismissing what Your own hands created, While smilin' on folks who out here movin' wicked?'
10.4: 'You see things like we do? You got human eyes now?'
10.5: 'You livin' life like a man with years to count? You aging like we do?'
10.6: 'Is that why You diggin' for my sins, Searchin' me like I'm tryna hide somethin'?'
10.7: 'But You already know I ain't wicked like that. And nobody can pull me out Your grip anyway.'
10.8: 'You the one who formed me with Your own hands— Piece by piece, all detailed and intentional. Now You tryna tear me down?'
10.9: 'Remember You made me from clay, right? You really just gon' break me back down to dust?'
10.10: 'Didn't You pour me out like milk, And turn me into cheese?'
10.11: 'Didn't You cover me with skin and muscle, Put my bones and veins all together like a knit sweater?'
10.12: 'You gave me life, showed me favor, And watched over my spirit this whole time.'
10.13: 'But deep down, You had this plan the whole time. I know You been sittin' on this.'
10.14: 'If I slip up, You record it. And You ain't lettin' no sin slide past You.'
10.15: 'If I'm wicked—yeah, I deserve this. But even if I'm righteous, I still gotta walk around with my head down. I'm covered in shame. Just look at my pain!'
10.16: 'If I do try to stand tall, You hunt me down like a wild lion, And flex Your power on me again.'
10.17: 'You keep bringin' new charges against me, Stackin' up Your anger, And I'm caught in non-stop chaos and battle.'
10.18: 'Why You even let me be born? I wish I had died before anybody laid eyes on me.'
10.19: 'It woulda been like I never existed. Straight from the womb to the grave—no middle.'
10.20: 'Ain't my days short already? Just let me be. Let me get some peace before it's over.'
10.21: 'Before I go to that place I ain't comin' back from— That shadow land, cold and dark.'
10.22: 'A place full of darkness on darkness, Where death's shadow rules, No order, no structure, And even the light there feel like darkness.'

11.1: Then Zophar the Naamathite jumped in and said,
11.2: 'You really think you can just talk non-stop and not get checked? All that chatter supposed to make you right?'
11.3: 'You think all this empty talk gon' keep folks quiet? You out here clownin'—nobody supposed to call you on it?'
11.4: 'You claim your beliefs are solid, That you clean in God's eyes.'
11.5: 'Man, I wish God would speak up, Just open His mouth and set things straight.'
11.6: 'If He showed you real wisdom—the deep stuff— You'd realize you ain't got it all figured out. And trust me, God ain't even givin' you the full payback for your sins.'
11.7: 'You think you can fully understand God? You think you can reach the edge of His greatness?'
11.8: 'His ways are higher than the sky—what you gon' do with that? They deeper than the grave—what could you possibly know?'
11.9: 'His knowledge? Longer than the earth, Wider than the ocean.'
11.10: 'If He decides to move, lock somebody up, or call court into session— Who gon' stop Him?'
11.11: 'He sees right through fake folks. He peep all the wickedness. You think He ain't gon' call it out?'
11.12: 'A foolish man talkin' like he wise? That's like a wild donkey havin' a baby that comes out human. Ain't happenin'.'
11.13: 'Look, Job—if you would get your heart right, Stretch your hands up to God in real surrender—'
11.14: 'If there's sin in your grip, let it go. Kick all that wickedness out your tent.'
11.15: 'Then you could look up with confidence, Stand firm with no fear.'
11.16: 'You'd forget all the mess you been through, It'd fade like water under the bridge.'
11.17: 'Your life would shine brighter than noon, Even your dark moments would look like sunrise.'
11.18: 'You'd feel secure, finally have hope. You could settle down and rest easy.'
11.19: 'You'd sleep in peace, no fear in sight. People would be knockin' just to get on your good side.'
11.20: 'But the wicked? Their vision gone. No escape, no future. Their only hope is death.'

12.2: 'Oh wow, look at y'all— Y'all must be the wise ones, huh? Guess wisdom gon' die when y'all do!'
12.3: 'I got sense too, don't get it twisted. I ain't beneath none of y'all. Everybody knows the stuff you just said.'
12.4: 'I'm the one gettin' clowned by my own friends— Even though I called on God and He answered. I been just and blameless, and y'all out here laughin' at me.'
12.5: 'Folks sittin' comfy don't respect the lamp of the struggler. They only prep it for folks who fallin'.'
12.6: 'Meanwhile, the tents of thieves stay winnin'. And the ones who test God? They livin' secure— With stuff God Himself provided.'
12.7: 'But go ask the animals—they'll school you. Birds in the sky? They'll break it down.'
12.8: 'Talk to the earth—it got lessons. The fish in the sea got a word for you too.'
12.9: 'All of 'em know—it's God's hand behind this.'
12.10: 'In His hand is the life of every living thing, And the breath of every human bein'.'
12.11: 'Just like your tongue know flavor, Your ears supposed to know truth.'
12.12: 'Wisdom comes with age, right? Long life's supposed to bring understanding.'
12.13: 'But real wisdom and strength? That's God's lane. He got all the strategy and knowledge.'
12.14: 'If He tear something down, you ain't buildin' it back. If He lock somebody up, they ain't gettin' free.'
12.15: 'If He holds back the waters, land dries out. If He lets them loose, they flood everything.'
12.16: 'He got all the power and the insight. Even the tricked and the ones doin' the trickin'? They both His.'
12.17: 'He snatches up counselors, leaves 'em robbed, Turns judges into straight fools.'
12.18: 'He takes the chains off kings, And straps 'em up tight with belts instead.'
12.19: 'He leads princes away with nothin', And topples the powerful like they ain't nothin'.'
12.20: 'He silences trusted voices, Takes the wisdom right outta the elders.'
12.21: 'He throws shame on rulers, And strips the strong of their weapons.'
12.22: 'He exposes deep secrets buried in the dark, Even death's shadow can't hide from Him.'
12.23: 'He can grow a nation or wipe it out. He can spread a people wide, or bring 'em back tight.'
12.24: 'He can take away the sense of leaders, Make 'em wander around like they lost in the wilderness.'
12.25: 'They feelin' around in the dark with no light, Stumblin' like drunk men—'cause He made it so.'

13.1: Look, I done seen all this with my own eyes, Heard it, took it in, and I understand.
13.2: Y'all ain't tellin' me nothin' new. I know what you know—I ain't beneath none of y'all.
13.3: But I wanna speak to God directly. I'm tryna have a real convo with the Almighty.
13.4: Y'all fake with it—spreading lies. A bunch of sorry doctors with no real medicine.
13.5: Man, if y'all would just shut up, That might be the wisest thing you ever did.
13.6: Now listen to me for real, Hear me out while I plead my case.
13.7: You gon' lie on God's behalf now? Say false things tryin' to defend Him?
13.8: You really tryna play favorites for God? Fightin' for Him like He need you to cover for Him?
13.9: You think He won't check you when He peeps it? You think you can clown Him like you clown a man?
13.10: He definitely gon' call y'all out If He catch you bein' shady behind the scenes.
13.11: Ain't His greatness enough to shake you? Ain't His presence enough to have you shook?
13.12: All that fake wisdom y'all spittin'? It's like ashes in the wind. Clay walls that can't hold up.
13.13: Be quiet and let me talk. Whatever happens after that, let it happen.
13.14: Why I'm risking it all like this? Why I'm holdin' my life in my own hands?
13.15: Even if He takes me out—I'm still gon' trust Him. But best believe I'ma still defend myself in front of Him.
13.16: He the only chance I got to be saved. A fake dude couldn't even stand in His presence.
13.17: So listen close to what I'm sayin'. Tune in to my words, loud and clear.
13.18: Look, I got my case ready. And I know I'ma be proven right.
13.19: Who else tryin' to argue with me? 'Cause if I stay silent now—I might as well be dead.
13.20: God, just don't do these two things, And I won't run from You.
13.21: First, take Your heavy hand off me. Second, don't let me be terrified of You.
13.22: Then You call, and I'll answer. Or let me speak first, and You respond.
13.23: Tell me what I did. List my sins, break it down for me.
13.24: Why You actin' distant? Why You treatin' me like I'm the enemy?
13.25: You out here crushin' me like I'm just a dead leaf blowin' in the wind? Chasin' me like I'm just dry stubble?
13.26: You writin' down harsh stuff against me, Makin' me pay for sins I did way back in the day.
13.27: You got my feet locked up, Watchin' my every step, Trackin' every move like I'm wearin' an ankle monitor.
13.28: Man ain't nothin'—we rot like spoiled meat, Like clothes moths done ate through.

14.1: Man born from a woman? His days short, and full of pain.
14.2: He come out like a flower—pretty for a second, Then he withers, gone like a shadow, just like that.
14.3: And You really got Your eyes on someone like that? You bring folks like me into court with You?
14.4: Who can pull something clean outta somethin' dirty? Ain't nobody.
14.5: You the One who set our days, Counted every month we get. You drew the line—we can't cross it.
14.6: So please, just look away for a minute, Let man rest till his shift's over like a hired hand.
14.7: Now a tree? Yeah, a tree got hope. You can chop it down and it still might grow back. New shoots pop off, keep reachin'.
14.8: Even if the roots get old in the dirt, Even if the stump look dead—
14.9: Just a whiff of water can bring it back. It'll bud and sprout like it was never cut.
14.10: But a man? He dies, lays down, Breathes his last—and where he at?
14.11: Like water dryin' up in the ocean, Like a riverbed goin' bone dry—
14.12: Man lays down and don't get back up. Not until the skies disappear. Ain't no wakin' up, no comin' back.
14.13: God, I wish You'd just hide me in the grave for a while, Keep me tucked away 'til Your anger cools off. Set a timer—and remember me later.
14.14: If a man dies… can he live again? I'd wait through all this hard service 'Til my change finally shows up.
14.15: You'd call me, and I'd answer You. You'd actually want me—Your own creation.
14.16: Right now, You keep track of every step I take… But You not watchin' over my sin, right?
14.17: You bagged up my wrongs, sealed it tight. Covered up all my mess.
14.18: But even mountains fall and crumble, Rocks get pushed from where they stand.
14.19: Water erodes stone, Floods wash away the soil— Same way You wash away man's hope.
14.20: You always win that battle. Man passes on. You shift his face, send him off.
14.21: His kids might rise up successful—he don't see it. They could fall—he don't know it.
14.22: But his body feels the ache, And his soul still mourns.

15.1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite clapped back and said,
15.2: 'You call yourself wise, but you talkin' nonsense— Just blowin' hot air like an east wind.'
15.3: 'You really out here reasonin' with empty words? Givin' speeches that help nobody?'
15.4: 'You done thrown out the fear of God, And stopped even tryin' to pray.'
15.5: 'Your own sin got you talkin' slick, You speakin' like somebody who manipulates truth.'
15.6: 'You don't need me to judge you— Your own mouth put you on blast. Your lips told on you.'
15.7: 'You was the first man ever born or somethin'? You older than the hills now?'
15.8: 'You think you the only one that heard from God? You hoardin' all the wisdom now?'
15.9: 'What you know that we don't? What insight you got that we ain't heard before?'
15.10: 'Look, we got gray-haired folks in the room, Old heads way older than your own daddy.'
15.11: 'God's comfort ain't enough for you? Even when He came at you soft, you still twisted?'
15.12: 'Why your heart driftin' off like that? Why your eyes flashin' like you know somethin' God don't?'
15.13: 'You turned your spirit against God, And now you talkin' reckless out your mouth.'
15.14: 'Man ain't pure—not by himself. Ain't nobody righteous just cause they born from a woman.'
15.15: 'God don't even put full trust in His angels, And even heaven gotta get cleaned up in His sight.'
15.16: 'So what about man—who stay filthy, Drinkin' sin down like it's water?'
15.17: 'Listen up—I'ma tell you what I seen with my own eyes.'
15.18: 'This what wise men passed down— No secrets held back from what their fathers taught.'
15.19: 'Them same folks who had the land to themselves, Way before outsiders ever touched it.'
15.20: 'The wicked stay in pain all their life. They don't know when their days gon' run out.'
15.21: 'Fear always in their ears, Even when things look good, destruction creepin' up.'
15.22: 'He don't believe he'll make it back from the dark— The sword already waitin' for him.'
15.23: 'He beggin' for food, askin', "Where it at?" But he knows trouble right around the corner.'
15.24: 'Panic and pressure stay on his neck, Crushing him like a king at war ready to attack.'
15.25: 'Why? 'Cause he dared to stretch his hand toward God, Actin' wild and bold against the Almighty.'
15.26: 'He ran at God full speed, Shield up, pride all over him.'
15.27: 'He sittin' up fat, proud of his wealth, Stomach full, waist wide—livin' large.'
15.28: 'But he chillin' in empty places, In houses nobody wanna live in— Buildings fallin' apart, about to be ruins.'
15.29: 'He won't stay rich. His wealth won't last. His empire won't spread across the land.'
15.30: 'He won't escape the darkness. God's breath gon' dry him out like fire on branches.'
15.31: 'He better not put his trust in foolish lies, 'Cause all he gon' get back is more foolishness.'
15.32: 'It'll all fall apart before its time. His fruit won't even have time to ripen.'
15.33: 'He'll drop what little he got—like grapes fallin' too early, Or olive blossoms droppin' off before harvest.'
15.34: 'People who play both sides? They end up empty. And the homes built on shady deals? Burnt to the ground.'
15.35: 'They stay birthin' trouble and bringin' out nothin'. They womb stay pregnant with lies.'

16.1: Then Job spoke up and said,
16.2: 'Man, I done heard all this before. Y'all some sorry comforters—every last one of you.'
16.3: 'Y'all just blowin' more hot air. Ain't you tired of talkin'? What got y'all so pressed to respond like this?'
16.4: 'If the shoe was on the other foot, I could talk just like y'all do. I could pile up words, shake my head, And judge you while you suffer.'
16.5: 'But nah—I'd try to speak life into you. I'd use my mouth to lift you up. My words would actually help ease your pain.'
16.6: 'But look—even when I talk, my pain don't let up. And if I stay quiet, I don't feel no better either.'
16.7: 'God done wore me out. And y'all helped destroy everybody that was left around me.'
16.8: 'I'm skin and bones now, Lookin' like my own body testifying against me.'
16.9: 'He rippin' me apart in anger, Gritting His teeth at me. God Himself feel like my enemy— Staring me down hard.'
16.10: 'People gawk at me with open mouths, Smack me in the face with no shame. They teamin' up against me like I deserve this.'
16.11: 'God handed me over to the wicked, Gave me to folks who don't care nothin' about Him.'
16.12: 'I was chillin'. Life was good. Then He snatched me by the neck and wrecked me— Used me for target practice.'
16.13: 'His archers all around me, Shootin' straight at my heart with no mercy. My guts spilled out on the ground.'
16.14: 'He hits me over and over, Breakin' me down like a soldier rushin' the line.'
16.15: 'I got sackcloth sewed into my skin, Laid my head down in the dirt—humble and broken.'
16.16: 'My face swollen from cryin', My eyes got death hangin' over them like a shadow.'
16.17: 'But I ain't done nothin' violent, And my prayers been real—pure from the heart.'
16.18: 'Earth, don't you cover my blood. Let my cry rise up and keep echoing.'
16.19: 'I know I got a witness up in heaven. Somebody got my file on record with God.'
16.20: 'My so-called friends mocking me… But I'm still cryin' my eyes out to the Lord.'
16.21: 'Man, I wish somebody would step in for me, Stand before God on my behalf— Like one friend pleading for another.'
16.22: 'Cause I ain't got many years left. I'm headed down a road I ain't comin' back from.'

17.1: "Man, my spirit is crushed. My days done burned out. The grave sittin' right there waitin' on me."
17.2: "Ain't I surrounded by mockers? All I see is people tryna provoke me."
17.3: "God, lock in a promise with me Yourself. Who else out here gon' vouch for me?"
17.4: "You done closed their hearts from understanding, So ain't no way You liftin' them up."
17.5: "Whoever flatters their friends to look good? Even their kids gon' suffer for it."
17.6: "But me? I became the joke of the streets. People spit in my face like I'm nothin'."
17.7: "My eyes weak from all this cryin', And my body? It's just skin and bones now."
17.8: "Good men look at this and get shook. Even the righteous rise up against fake folks."
17.9: "Still, the real ones gon' keep walkin' right, And folks with clean hands? They gon' come out stronger."
17.10: "But y'all? Y'all can go 'head and circle back, 'Cause I ain't seen a single wise man in this crew."
17.11: "My time's up. All the plans I had? Gone. Even my deepest dreams feel broken."
17.12: "Y'all out here callin' night 'day,' Sayin' 'The light's comin!' while it's still pitch dark."
17.13: "If I start waitin' on the grave like it's home, Lay down in the dark like it's my bed—"
17.14: "If I tell rot and decay, 'You my daddy,' And call the worms, 'Mama' and 'Sis'—"
17.15: "Then tell me—what hope I got left? Who out here can even see it?"
17.16: "That hope? It's headed down to Sheol. Me and it gon' be buried together in the dirt."

18.1: Then Bildad the Shuhite spoke up and said,
18.2: 'How long you gon' keep talkin'? Try gettin' some sense, then maybe we can talk.'
18.3: 'Why you actin' like we dumb animals? Like we slow or somethin' in your eyes?'
18.4: 'You tearin' yourself up with all that rage— You think the world supposed to stop for you? Mountains supposed to move just 'cause you mad?'
18.5: 'The light of the wicked gon' go out. Their fire won't shine no more.'
18.6: 'It's gon' be dark in their house, Even their lamp on the table gon' die.'
18.7: 'They used to walk strong, But now their own plans trip 'em up.'
18.8: 'They get caught in their own trap, Walk right into a net they set for somebody else.'
18.9: 'The trap snatch them by the heel, And a snare grab 'em with no warning.'
18.10: 'There's a noose hidin' in the dirt, And a trap waitin' right in the road.'
18.11: 'Terror be on every side, Pushin' him up out his comfort zone.'
18.12: 'His strength gon' dry up, And destruction waitin' right next to him.'
18.13: 'Disease gon' eat away at his skin, Death itself gon' chew through his limbs.'
18.14: 'He'll be dragged out his home, Presented to the king of terrors like a show.'
18.15: 'Strangers gon' move into his tent, And fire and sulfur gon' rain down on what's left.'
18.16: 'His roots rot beneath, And the branches up top wither and die.'
18.17: 'Nobody gon' remember his name, And he won't be on no honor roll.'
18.18: 'He gon' be pushed outta the light, Sent into the dark, exiled from the world.'
18.19: 'He ain't got no sons, no legacy, Nobody left behind to carry his name.'
18.20: 'Folks out west gon' be shocked when they hear, And folks out east? They gon' tremble.'
18.21: 'That's what happens to the wicked— That's what comes to people who don't even know God.'

19.1: Then Job spoke up and said,
19.2: 'How long y'all gon' keep tormentin' my soul, Crushin' me over and over with your words?'
19.3: 'Y'all done disrespected me ten times now. Ain't even ashamed of how wrong you've done me.'
19.4: 'Even if I did mess up, That's between me and God—it's my burden, not yours.'
19.5: 'But if y'all keep talkin' down on me, Usin' my pain to lift yourselves up—'
19.6: 'Then understand this: God the One who did this to me. He caught me up in a net I can't get out of.'
19.7: 'I cry out, "This ain't right!"—but nobody hears me. I shout for justice, but it don't come.'
19.8: 'He blocked off all my exits. It's dark no matter where I turn.'
19.9: 'He stripped me of my honor, Snatched the crown right off my head.'
19.10: 'He's breaking me down from every angle, And now I'm just a shell. He tore up my hope like a tree pulled up by the roots.'
19.11: 'He lit His anger against me, And now I'm treated like I'm His enemy.'
19.12: 'His troops surround me. They build up their ramp like I'm a city under siege. They camping out all around my tent.'
19.13: 'He made my brothers dip out on me. Even folks I used to know don't rock with me no more.'
19.14: 'My family turned their back, And my day-ones forgot all about me.'
19.15: 'People in my house, even my servants— They treat me like I'm a stranger, like I don't belong.'
19.16: 'I call my worker and he won't even answer. I'm out here beggin' like I ain't his master.'
19.17: 'My own wife can't stand to smell my breath. My own kids look at me like I'm nasty.'
19.18: 'Even little kids clown me. Soon as I get up, they talk trash.'
19.19: 'All my close ones? They hate me now. Even the ones I used to love done flipped on me.'
19.20: 'My bones barely holdin' on to my skin. I only escaped death by the skin of my teeth.'
19.21: 'Please... have some mercy on me, y'all— God already struck me down!'
19.22: 'Why y'all actin' like God's tag team? Ain't my suffering enough for you already?'
19.23: 'Man, I wish my words were written down... Put in a book for real.'
19.24: 'Better yet—engraved in stone with an iron tool and lead, So they never fade.'
19.25: ''Cause I know my Redeemer lives. And one day He gon' stand right here on this earth.'
19.26: 'Even if my skin get destroyed, I know I'ma see God in this body.'
19.27: 'I'ma see Him for myself. With my own two eyes, not nobody else's. Man... my heart can barely take it just thinkin' about it.'
19.28: 'So if y'all still plottin', sayin', "How can we break him more?"— Just know this whole thing runs deep. The root is in me.'
19.29: 'Y'all better watch out for that sword, though. 'Cause God's wrath ain't no joke. It brings judgment—and you need to know, It's comin'.'

20.1: Then Zophar the Naamathite clapped back and said,
20.2: 'I gotta speak on this—my thoughts won't let me stay quiet. I'm stirred up deep inside.'
20.3: 'I heard your little shots at me, And my spirit can't sit still—I gotta respond.'
20.4: 'Ain't this somethin' everybody knows? Since back when man first hit the earth—'
20.5: 'That the wicked might win for a minute, But their joy don't last long.'
20.6: 'Even if they act all high and mighty, Reachin' for the skies, head in the clouds—'
20.7: 'They still gon' vanish forever like waste flushed away. People gon' look around like, "Where he at?"'
20.8: 'Gone like a dream when you wake up. Like a night vision you can't hold on to.'
20.9: 'You saw him once, but never again. He won't show up where he used to be.'
20.10: 'His kids gon' be out here beggin' the poor for help, And whatever he stacked up? He gotta give it back.'
20.11: 'He might've had energy in his youth, But it's all gon' lay down with him in the dirt.'
20.12: 'He might've loved evil like it was candy, Keepin' it tucked under his tongue—real close.'
20.13: 'Holdin' on tight, never lettin' go, Tastin' it like it's sweet.'
20.14: 'But when it hit his stomach? It turns. Turns into cobra venom.'
20.15: 'He swallowed riches, But he gon' throw 'em right back up— God gon' snatch 'em out his belly.'
20.16: 'He suckin' poison now, Snake bites gon' finish him off.'
20.17: 'He won't see rivers of honey and milk, Ain't no sweet reward waitin' for him.'
20.18: 'He might work for it, but he ain't keepin' it. All that effort? No satisfaction.'
20.19: 'Why? 'Cause he crushed the poor and walked away, Took homes he ain't even build.'
20.20: 'He never knew peace inside, And couldn't hold on to nothin' he wanted.'
20.21: 'Ain't nothin' left for him to enjoy, So his little moment of success won't stick.'
20.22: 'Even when he feelin' full of himself, Pain and pressure gon' close in from all sides.'
20.23: 'Just when he about to eat good, God gon' drop His fury— Rain down wrath mid-bite.'
20.24: 'He might dodge one weapon, But the bronze arrow gon' pierce straight through.'
20.25: 'That sharp arrow stickin' out his gut— And now terror comin' in heavy.'
20.26: 'All his treasures? Covered in darkness. An untamed fire gon' eat up everything he left behind.'
20.27: 'Heaven itself gon' expose him, And the earth ain't lettin' him slide either.'
20.28: 'All his riches gon' dip, Gone with the wind in the day God brings wrath.'
20.29: 'That's what God got lined up for wicked folks. That's their inheritance—straight from the Lord.'

21.2: 'Y'all need to really listen this time. Let that be the one good thing y'all do for me.'
21.3: 'Let me talk, just for a minute. Then go 'head and keep jokin' if you must.'
21.4: 'Look—my issue ain't with people. But even if it was, don't I got a right to be upset?'
21.5: 'Take a look at me. For real. You'd be shook too—hand over your mouth type shook.'
21.6: 'Even when I think about it, I start trembling. My body reacts to the memory.'
21.7: 'So tell me—why the wicked livin' long? Why they get to grow old and powerful?'
21.8: 'Their kids steady thrivin' right in front of 'em, Whole families locked in and doin' good.'
21.9: 'They homes peaceful, no fear in sight, And God's rod ain't even touchin' 'em.'
21.10: 'Their bulls ain't missin' no breedin', Their cows birthin' calves easy, no issues.'
21.11: 'They let their kids run free like sheep, Lil ones dancin' and wildin' out.'
21.12: 'They singin' with tambourines and harps, Turnin' up to flutes like they at a celebration.'
21.13: 'They livin' the good life all the way, Then just drop dead in an instant—no struggle.'
21.14: 'And yet they say to God, "Get away from us, We don't need You or Your ways."'
21.15: 'They like, "Who's the Almighty? Why should we serve Him? What's the benefit in even prayin' to Him?"'
21.16: 'But their success? That ain't even in their control. And me? I want nothing to do with their lifestyle.'
21.17: 'So how often do the wicked really get cut off? How often God hit them with that kind of judgment?'
21.18: 'Y'all say they blow away like dust in the wind, But that storm don't hit when y'all say it will.'
21.19: 'Y'all claim God saves their punishment for their kids— But nah, let them feel it. Let them see it firsthand.'
21.20: 'Let him look destruction dead in the face. Let him drink God's wrath himself.'
21.21: 'Why he care about his family after he gone, When his time already been cut short?'
21.22: 'Y'all really think y'all can teach God somethin'? He the One judgin' heaven—it don't get higher than that.'
21.23: 'One dude dies strong, full of life, Everything goin' smooth and secure.'
21.24: 'His fridge stocked, bones feelin' good, Body strong, no struggle.'
21.25: 'Another dies bitter, Never got to enjoy a good meal or a good moment.'
21.26: 'But both of 'em end up in the same dirt. Worms cover 'em just the same.'
21.27: 'I know what y'all thinkin'. I see right through the way y'all plottin' to twist my situation.'
21.28: 'Y'all say, "Where the house at? Where's the tent of that wicked man?"'
21.29: 'But have you asked people who actually travel? Don't you see the signs they point to?'
21.30: 'The wicked? They bein' saved for judgment day. Yeah, they gon' get brought out—but not when you say.'
21.31: 'Ain't nobody checkin' 'em to their face. Nobody holdin' them accountable while they here.'
21.32: 'But they still get buried with respect, People even postin' up outside the tomb.'
21.33: 'They get laid down easy in the valley, And folks still line up to follow behind, Like everybody else before them.'
21.34: 'So how y'all gon' comfort me with empty talk, When all y'all got is lies and weak logic?'

22.1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite spoke up and said,
22.2: 'What you think—man can be useful to God? Even a wise man only helps himself.'
22.3: 'You think God gets hype 'cause you act righteous? You think it profits Him when you try to walk straight?'
22.4: 'So you say He correcting you just 'cause you fear Him? Nah. That ain't why He puttin' you on trial.'
22.5: 'Let's be real—your sin run deep. Your wickedness got no end.'
22.6: 'You took stuff from your own brother for no reason, Stripped poor folks of what little they had to wear.'
22.7: 'You ain't give tired people no water. And hungry folks? You left 'em starvin.'
22.8: 'You let the rich man run things, Let the "important" people take over.'
22.9: 'You turned away widows empty-handed, And crushed orphans with no strength to fight back.'
22.10: 'That's why traps are all around you now, And sudden fear got you shook.'
22.11: 'You blinded by darkness, can't see nothin'. It's like you drownin' in deep water.'
22.12: 'Ain't God way up high in the heavens? You see how high them stars sit?'
22.13: 'But you act like, "What God gon' know? He can't see through all this darkness."'
22.14: 'You say, "Clouds too thick for Him to peep what I'm doin'." Like He walkin' on top of the sky, far removed.'
22.15: 'You still walkin' the same path the wicked did back then— The ones who got taken out early?'
22.16: 'Foundations washed away like they never existed.'
22.17: 'They told God, "Move around! We don't need You." Like the Almighty couldn't touch 'em.'
22.18: 'But look—God still filled their houses with good stuff. Even though their whole mindset? I stay far from that.'
22.19: 'The righteous see what happened and celebrate. The innocent laugh like, "Told you so."'
22.20: 'They say, "Our enemies done fell off. Fire wiped out whatever was left of 'em."'
22.21: 'Now listen—get close to God and be at peace. That's how good things'll come your way.'
22.22: 'Take in what He say, Store His words deep in your heart.'
22.23: 'If you come back to the Almighty, He'll build you up again. Just kick sin out your space.'
22.24: 'Then you'll treat gold like dirt, Even the gold from Ophir like pebbles in the stream.'
22.25: 'The Lord Himself will be your treasure— Your silver and your gold.'
22.26: 'Then you'll take joy in the Almighty, And lift your face straight up to Him.'
22.27: 'You'll pray to Him—He'll hear you. And you'll come through on your promises.'
22.28: 'You'll speak things into existence, And God'll establish it. Light gon' shine on everything you do.'
22.29: 'When folks try to throw you down, you'll say, "I'm goin' up!" And God gon' lift up the humble.'
22.30: 'He'll even rescue folks who guilty— Just 'cause your hands stay clean.'

23.2: 'Even today, I'm still complainin'—and it hurts. I'm worn out from all this groanin'.'
23.3: 'Man… if only I knew where to find Him. I'd walk straight up to God's throne.'
23.4: 'I'd lay my case out right in front of Him, Fill my mouth with everything I've been holdin' in.'
23.5: 'I'd listen to what He got to say back, Try to understand His answer.'
23.6: 'You think He'd just crush me with His power? Nah—He'd actually listen.'
23.7: 'Somebody walkin' upright could speak with Him, And I'd finally be free—for good—from my Judge.'
23.8: 'But I look to the front—He ain't there. Look behind me—I still don't see Him.'
23.9: 'He movin' on the left side, but I can't catch Him. He shiftin' to the right—I still can't spot Him.'
23.10: 'But He know the path I'm walkin'. And when He's done testin' me? I'ma come out like pure gold.'
23.11: 'I been walkin' steady in His steps. Ain't turned away from His way.'
23.12: 'I ain't ignored what He said— Matter fact, I hold His words closer than food.'
23.13: 'But He God. Ain't nobody changin' His mind. Whatever He want? That's what gon' happen.'
23.14: 'He fulfillin' what He planned for me. And He got more in store I don't even know about.'
23.15: 'That's why I'm shook when I think about Him. When I really sit with it? I'm scared.'
23.16: 'God got my heart feelin' weak. The Almighty got me terrified.'
23.17: 'Cause He ain't cut me off from the dark— He let me stare it straight in the face.'

24.1: If God really sees everything, Why folks who claim to know Him can't even see His justice play out?
24.2: People out here movin' boundary lines, Stealin' sheep and eatin' off somebody else's flock.
24.3: They snatch up the orphans' donkeys, Take the widow's ox like it's collateral.
24.4: They shove poor folks off the road, Force the needy to go into hidin'.
24.5: Like wild donkeys in the desert, These folks out here grindin', searchin' for food. Whatever the wilderness gives 'em, they use to feed their babies.
24.6: They gather scraps in the field, Pick up leftovers in the vineyards owned by the wicked.
24.7: They sleep outside with nothin' on, No clothes to cover them from the cold.
24.8: Soaked by mountain rain, They curl up by rocks 'cause they ain't got no shelter.
24.9: They snatch babies away from their mamas, Take pledges from folks who ain't got nothin' to give.
24.10: They make the poor walk around naked, Take food right out their hands even when they starving.
24.11: They crush olives inside the walls of rich folks, Tread out wine—but they still thirsty themselves.
24.12: The dying groanin' in the streets, The wounded cryin' out—but God ain't holdin' nobody accountable for it.
24.13: Some folks rebel against the light, Don't wanna know God's ways, Ain't tryna walk in His truth.
24.14: Murderers get up with the sunrise, Kill the poor and needy in broad daylight— Then sneak around at night like thieves.
24.15: Adulterers wait for the dark, Tell themselves, 'Ain't nobody gon' see me.' They cover their faces to stay hidden.
24.16: They break into houses after sunset, Ones they been scoping out all day. They want no part of the light.
24.17: Sunrise don't mean nothin' to them— It's just another version of death's shadow. If somebody recognizes them? They panic in fear.
24.18: They move fast like water, But their legacy should be cursed, Nobody should ever follow their trail.
24.19: Just like heat dries up snow water, Death gon' swallow them up too.
24.20: Nobody gon' remember them. Worms gon' eat 'em like dessert. They legacy dead— Their wickedness snapped off like a broken branch.
24.21: They prey on the childless, Ignore the widow, Do nothin' but harm.
24.22: But God still got the power to snatch the mighty away. Even when they rise up, they got no control over life.
24.23: He lets them feel secure for a while, But His eyes stay locked on every move they make.
24.24: They might rise up for a minute, But just like that—they gone. Brought low, laid to rest like everybody else. They dry up like cut wheat.
24.25: So if I'm lyin'? Prove me wrong. Show me that anything I said ain't true.

25.1: Then Bildad the Shuhite spoke up and said,
25.2: 'Power and fear? Yeah, that all belongs to God. He keeps everything in check up in heaven.'
25.3: 'Ain't no countin' His armies, And His light shines on everybody.'
25.4: 'So how can man ever claim to be right before God? How can somebody born from a woman say they pure?'
25.5: 'Even the moon don't shine right to Him, And the stars? They don't look clean in His eyes either.'
25.6: 'So what that make us? Humans? We like maggots. Sons of man? Just worms in comparison.'

26.2: 'Wow. You really helped the powerless, huh? You really saved the one who ain't got no strength?'
26.3: 'You gave advice to folks without wisdom? Shared deep insight with the world, huh?'
26.4: 'Tell me—who you even talkin' to? And what spirit was behind your words?'
26.5: 'Even the dead tremble, Those under the water, and whatever lives down there.'
26.6: 'The grave? Wide open to God. Destruction can't hide from Him either.'
26.7: 'He stretches out the skies over nothin', And hangs the whole earth on nothin.'
26.8: 'He holds up water in thick clouds, But the clouds don't even burst from the weight.'
26.9: 'He covers His throne with clouds, Hidin' His glory behind the veil.'
26.10: 'He drew a perfect circle on the water's surface, Where light and dark divide.'
26.11: 'Even the pillars of heaven shake When He speaks—His voice got that kind of power.'
26.12: 'He stirs the sea with raw force, And with wisdom, He breaks storms apart.'
26.13: 'His Spirit dressed the heavens with beauty, And His hand pierced the fleeing serpent.'
26.14: 'But all that? That's just the edge of what He can do. A whisper of His greatness. So who can even begin to grasp the thunder of His full power?'

27.2: 'As surely as God lives—the One who took away my justice, The Almighty who left my soul feelin' bitter—'
27.3: 'As long as I'm still breathin', And God's breath is still in my lungs—'
27.4: 'I ain't gon' lie with my mouth, And I ain't gon' twist truth with my tongue.'
27.5: 'I'll never say y'all were right about me. I'd rather die than throw away my integrity.'
27.6: 'I'm holdin' tight to my righteousness—ain't lettin' it go. My heart won't shame me for how I've lived.'
27.7: 'Let my enemy be counted like the wicked, And the one tryna take me down be like the unrighteous.'
27.8: 'What hope do fake folks got, even if they rich, When God steps in to take their life?'
27.9: 'You think God gon' hear them when trouble shows up? You think they really lean on Him like that?'
27.10: 'Do they even love the Almighty? Do they call on Him constantly? I doubt it.'
27.11: 'Let me break it down for you—how God really works. I ain't holdin' back what I know about the Almighty.'
27.12: 'Y'all done seen this yourselves— So why y'all still out here talkin' reckless?'
27.13: 'This what the wicked get from God. This is what the oppressor inherits from the Almighty:'
27.14: 'Even if he got a gang of kids, They just bein' lined up for the sword. His offspring gon' still go hungry.'
27.15: 'The few that survive? They gon' die off too, And their wives won't even cry for 'em.'
27.16: 'He might stack silver like dirt, And hoard clothes like clay—'
27.17: 'But the righteous gon' end up wearin' that, And the innocent gon' split that silver.'
27.18: 'His house flimsy, like somethin' a moth would live in— Or a lil shack a guard threw together real quick.'
27.19: 'He might die rich, But he won't be remembered. He opens his eyes—and he gone.'
27.20: 'Fear gon' hit him like a flood, And a storm gon' snatch him up in the middle of the night.'
27.21: 'That east wind? It sweeps him away like trash, Pulls him right up outta his spot.'
27.22: 'That wind don't care—it don't hold back. He runnin' from it like it's chasin' him down.'
27.23: 'People gon' clap at his downfall, And hiss at him as he disappears for good.'

28.1: 'People know where to dig up silver, And there's a spot where gold gets purified.'
28.2: 'They pull iron straight out the ground, And melt copper from raw ore.'
28.3: 'Man puts an end to darkness, Digs deep into shadows and danger to find treasure.'
28.4: 'He cuts tunnels where nobody lives, In places no foot touches— Folks hang from ropes swingin' back and forth, Diggin' in the unknown.'
28.5: 'The earth gives us bread up top, But underneath, it's flipped like fire got ahold of it.'
28.6: 'The rocks got sapphires in 'em, And dust laced with gold.'
28.7: 'Ain't no bird ever seen that path, Not even a hawk with sharp eyes.'
28.8: 'Lions don't walk there, Not even the boldest beast crosses it.'
28.9: 'Humans put their hands on solid rock, Breakin' mountains from the roots up.'
28.10: 'They cut through stone to make water run, And their eyes spot every hidden gem.'
28.11: 'They block streams from flowin'— Pullin' out what's been hid deep underground.'
28.12: 'But hold up—where's wisdom at though? Where do you even go to get understanding?'
28.13: 'People don't know its value, And it ain't sittin' out here among the livin.'
28.14: 'The ocean say, "It ain't in me." The sea say, "Don't look here."'
28.15: 'You can't buy it with gold, Or weigh it out in silver.'
28.16: 'It ain't worth Ophir's gold, Or onyx, or sapphire gems.'
28.17: 'Ain't no gold or crystal match it. You can't trade it for the finest jewelry.'
28.18: 'Coral? Quartz? Don't even bring 'em up. Wisdom costs more than rubies.'
28.19: 'Topaz from Ethiopia can't compete, And even pure gold don't measure up.'
28.20: 'So again—where's wisdom come from? Where's understanding hiding?'
28.21: 'It's hidden from every living soul, Even birds flying high don't know where it's at.'
28.22: 'Destruction and Death say, "We heard about it… but only through whispers."'
28.23: 'God the only one who truly understands it. He knows exactly where wisdom stays.'
28.24: 'He looks from one end of the earth to the other, Sees everything under the skies.'
28.25: 'He weighed out the wind, Measured water like it came with a scale.'
28.26: 'He laid down rules for rain, And made paths for lightning to strike.'
28.27: 'That's when He saw wisdom, Spoke it out, locked it in, And searched it deep.'
28.28: 'And to humans, He said this right here: "Fearin' the Lord? That's wisdom. Walkin' away from evil? That's understanding."'

29.2: 'Man… I wish I could go back to the old days, Back when God had His eyes on me.'
29.3: 'When His light stayed on my head, And I walked through dark times still covered in His glow.'
29.4: 'Back in my prime, When God's presence felt like home inside my tent.'
29.5: 'When the Almighty was rollin' with me, And my kids were all around me.'
29.6: 'My path was flowin' with cream, And rocks drippin' oil like blessings that wouldn't stop.'
29.7: 'When I pulled up to the city gates, Sat down at the square with authority—'
29.8: 'Young dudes backed off when they saw me, And the old heads stood up outta respect.'
29.9: 'Even princes stopped talkin', Covered their mouths mid-sentence.'
29.10: 'The top leaders got quiet, Tongues stuck to the roof of their mouths.'
29.11: 'If folks heard me, they blessed me. If they saw me, they nodded with approval.'
29.12: 'Why? 'Cause I helped the poor who cried out, And the orphan with no one to back 'em up.'
29.13: 'People on their last breath still prayed blessings over me, And I made widows sing with joy again.'
29.14: 'I wore righteousness like a fitted outfit, Justice wrapped around me like a robe and crown.'
29.15: 'I was eyes for the blind, And legs for those who couldn't walk.'
29.16: 'I was like a father to the struggling, And I looked into cases that no one else touched.'
29.17: 'I broke the teeth of the wicked, Snatched victims right out their mouth.'
29.18: 'I used to say, "I'ma die right here in my nest, Grow old and live long like the grains of sand."'
29.19: 'My roots ran deep in the water, And my branches stayed fresh with dew all night.'
29.20: 'My strength never left me, My influence stayed sharp like a ready bow.'
29.21: 'People listened when I spoke. They waited quietly for my advice.'
29.22: 'When I talked, no one questioned me. My words hit like dew, gentle but weighty.'
29.23: 'They waited for me like rain in dry season, Opened their mouths like thirsty ground.'
29.24: 'Even when I joked, they barely believed it, 'Cause my presence was always serious and steady.'
29.25: 'I was the one leadin' the way, Sittin' like a king among soldiers— The one who brought comfort when folks were cryin'.'

30.1: 'But now? Young dudes clownin' me— Ones whose fathers I wouldn't even trust to watch my dogs.'
30.2: 'What strength do they even got left? They ain't got nothin' I could use.'
30.3: 'They skin and bones from hunger, Runnin' wild out in the wastelands, lookin' for scraps.'
30.4: 'They pickin' wild leaves off bushes, Diggin' up tree roots just to survive.'
30.5: 'Society kicked 'em out long ago— Folks yelled at them like they was thieves.'
30.6: 'Now they livin' in valleys and caves, Hidin' in cracks in the earth.'
30.7: 'They screamin' under bushes, Tryna stay warm beneath weeds and nettles.'
30.8: 'These the kids of fools, Sons of nobodies, Outcasts that got driven out.'
30.9: 'Now I'm the one they joke about. I'm their punchline.'
30.10: 'They can't stand me. They keep their distance, But don't think twice about spittin' in my face.'
30.11: 'Ever since God took His hand off me, They got bold—no respect at all.'
30.12: 'Mob of nobodies risin' up on my right side, Trippin' me up, plottin' ways to take me down.'
30.13: 'They tear up the path I walk, Push me deeper into this pain. Ain't nobody stoppin' them.'
30.14: 'They come at me like waves crashin' down, Rollin' over me like a storm that don't let up.'
30.15: 'Fear got me cornered now. My reputation gone with the wind, My good days disappeared like a cloud.'
30.16: 'My soul poured out—I got nothin' left. Affliction got a grip on me, and won't let go.'
30.17: 'At night, my bones scream. This pain? It never clocks out.'
30.18: 'My clothes twisted tight from the swelling. Feels like they stranglin' me like a tight collar.'
30.19: 'God threw me into the dirt, Now I'm like ashes, nothin' but dust.'
30.20: 'I cry out to You, but You don't answer. I stand here beggin', but You ain't respondin'.'
30.21: 'You turned on me, God. You hittin' me hard with Your own hands.'
30.22: 'You picked me up like wind in a storm, Then dropped me from the sky—no mercy.'
30.23: 'I know where this headed— You gon' take me to the grave, The place everybody ends up.'
30.24: 'Would You really crush a man already broken? Would You ignore the cry of someone already destroyed?''
30.25: 'Ain't I always wept for folks in pain? Didn't my soul grieve for the poor?'
30.26: 'But when I looked for good, evil came. When I waited for light, darkness pulled up instead.'
30.27: 'My heart stay in chaos. Affliction keep knockin' on my door every day.'
30.28: 'I walk around mournin' in silence, Cryin' out in the crowd, but no one helps.'
30.29: 'I'm livin' like jackals do, Hangin' with ostriches in the wild.'
30.30: 'My skin turnin' black and fallin' off, Bones on fire—burnin' up with fever.'
30.31: 'My harp don't sing no more—it mourns. My flute cryin' now, like it's weepin' with me.'

31.1: 'I made a deal with my eyes— I wasn't out here lustin' after young women.'
31.2: 'What's God supposed to give somebody who wilds out like that? What inheritance the Almighty got for the unfaithful?'
31.3: 'Ain't it destruction for the wicked, And disaster for the ones out here schemin'?'
31.4: 'Ain't God watchin' every move I make, Countin' every single step?'
31.5: 'If I ever walked in lies, Or was quick to deceive—'
31.6: 'Then weigh me on scales that don't lie. Let God see I kept it real.'
31.7: 'If I stepped off the righteous path, Chased after what my eyes wanted, Or had dirty hands—'
31.8: 'Then let me plant crops and someone else eat 'em. Let my whole harvest get pulled up by the roots.'
31.9: 'If I was out here lustin' after someone else's woman, Or posted up outside her door—'
31.10: 'Then let another man take my wife. Let her serve someone else instead of me.'
31.11: 'That would be wickedness, A sin worthy of judgment.'
31.12: 'It'd be like a fire that consumes everything, Burnin' up everything I worked for.'
31.13: 'If I ignored my servants when they complained, And acted like they voice ain't matter—'
31.14: 'What would I say when God stands up to question me? How could I even answer?'
31.15: 'Ain't we all made by the same God in the womb? Ain't the same hands form all of us?'
31.16: 'If I ever turned away the poor, Or made a widow cry from disappointment—'
31.17: 'If I kept my food to myself, And didn't let the fatherless eat with me—'
31.18: 'Even though I raised orphans like a father, And looked after widows since I was a kid—'
31.19: 'If I saw someone freezin' with no coat, And just kept walkin'—'
31.20: 'If they ain't bless me for keepin' them warm With my sheep's wool—'
31.21: 'If I ever raised my hand against the fatherless, Just 'cause I knew I had legal backup at the gate—'
31.22: 'Then let my arm break off. Let it fall from the socket for real.'
31.23: 'God's judgment terrifies me, And His majesty? I couldn't stand under it.'
31.24: 'If I ever put my hope in gold, Told fine jewelry, "You my security"—'
31.25: 'If I bragged on my wealth, Or flexed 'cause my hustle stacked up—'
31.26: 'If I saw the sun shining or the moon glowing And caught feelings like it was something to worship—'
31.27: 'And let my heart get seduced, And kissed my hand like I was blessing myself—'
31.28: 'Then yeah, that'd be a sin worth judging. 'Cause I'd be denying the God above.'
31.29: 'If I celebrated when my enemies fell, Or smiled when they got what was comin'—'
31.30: 'I swear I never let my mouth curse 'em, Didn't even wish harm on their soul.'
31.31: 'My people can testify: Ain't nobody in my house ever lacked a meal.'
31.32: 'I never let a stranger sleep outside, My door was always open to the traveler.'
31.33: 'If I tried to cover my sins like Adam did, Hidin' guilt in my chest—'
31.34: 'If I stayed silent outta fear of public shame, Scared of what people would say—'
31.35: 'Man... I wish somebody would just listen to me! Here I stand. I sign my name to all this.'
31.36: 'If God would answer, I'd wear His response like a crown on my head.'
31.37: 'I'd walk up to Him like a prince, Telling Him every step I ever took.'
31.38: 'If my land cries out against me, If the fields I worked are mournin'—'
31.39: 'If I stole from the ground, Or made the workers starve while I got rich—'
31.40: 'Then let thorns grow instead of wheat, And let weeds come up instead of barley.' The words of Job are done.

32.1: So Job's three friends finally stopped talkin'— 'Cause Job was standin' firm, convinced he was right.
32.2: But Elihu—son of Barachel the Buzite, from the fam of Ram— He was heated. Mad at Job for tryna justify himself instead of God.
32.3: And he was mad at the three friends too, 'Cause they couldn't come up with no real answer, Yet still tried to drag Job like he was wrong.
32.4: Elihu had been holdin' his tongue, 'Cause they were older than him—way older.
32.5: But when he saw they had nothin' left to say, His spirit flared up—he couldn't take it no more.
32.6: So Elihu, son of Barachel the Buzite, spoke up and said: 'I'm young, and y'all got years on me, So I was scared to jump in.'
32.7: 'I figured, "Let the elders speak first. They got age—they should have the wisdom."'
32.8: 'But nah—real understanding comes from the spirit God put in us. It's the breath of the Almighty that gives insight.'
32.9: 'Just 'cause you old don't mean you wise. Just 'cause you been around don't mean you understand what's right.'
32.10: 'So now it's my turn. Y'all gon' listen to me. I'm about to drop my opinion too.'
32.11: 'I waited and gave y'all space to talk, Listened while y'all tried to reason it out.'
32.12: 'I paid attention to every word, But none of y'all shut Job down. Y'all ain't answer him—not once.'
32.13: 'So don't even try to say, "We got wisdom—God will handle him." Nah, y'all ain't do that—y'all failed.'
32.14: 'Job ain't even talkin' to me yet, So I'm not comin' with the same tired arguments y'all used.'
32.15: 'They stuck now—no words left. Mouths shut. Minds blank.'
32.16: 'I waited long enough. Y'all had your turn. You stood still—no answers.'
32.17: 'So now I'ma speak. Time for me to drop my side.'
32.18: 'I'm full of things to say— This spirit inside me won't let me sit quiet.'
32.19: 'I feel like a bottle of wine about to pop— Like new wineskins about to burst open.'
32.20: 'I gotta speak to let this out. I can't hold back no more—I need relief.'
32.21: 'But don't expect me to play favorites. I ain't about to flatter nobody.'
32.22: 'I don't even know how to flatter, And if I did, God would check me real quick.'

33.1: 'Alright now, Job—listen up. Really hear me out and catch everything I'm sayin'.'
33.2: 'I'm openin' my mouth right now, My tongue is movin'—I got somethin' to say.'
33.3: 'What I'm bringin' comes from a sincere heart, And my lips speak truth—real wisdom.'
33.4: 'God's Spirit made me, And the breath of the Almighty gave me life.'
33.5: 'If you got a response, cool—say it. Stand up and speak your piece.'
33.6: 'But just so you know, I'm not above you. I'm made of clay too—we both human.'
33.7: 'So don't trip—I ain't here to scare you. I ain't about to weigh you down or come at you heavy.'
33.8: 'Now I been listenin', Job. I heard what you said—word for word.'
33.9: 'You said, "I'm clean, I ain't did nothin' wrong. I'm innocent—there's no sin on me."'
33.10: "'But God out here lookin' for reasons to charge me, Treatin' me like I'm His enemy.'"
33.11: "'He got my feet locked up, And He trackin' my every step.'"
33.12: 'Now hold up—on that part, you ain't right. Let me tell you why—God is way bigger than us.'
33.13: 'Why you fightin' with God? He ain't gotta explain every move He makes.'
33.14: 'God be speakin'—sometimes one way, sometimes another— But people just don't catch it.'
33.15: 'Maybe it's in a dream, A vision in the night while you sleepin' in bed.'
33.16: 'That's when He opens folks' ears And drops instruction straight into the soul.'
33.17: 'To stop somebody from messin' up, To humble 'em, bring 'em low before they go too far.'
33.18: 'He's protectin' their soul from destruction, Keepin' them from dyin' by the sword.'
33.19: 'But sometimes it ain't dreams—it's pain. God'll lay a man down with sickness and suffering.'
33.20: 'He loses his appetite, Can't even stand to look at food.'
33.21: 'His body shrinks, skin clingin' to bone. You can see bones that used to be hidden.'
33.22: 'He gets real close to death, Like executioners waitin' in the wings.'
33.23: 'But if there's a messenger— Someone who can step in, speak truth, and show the way—'
33.24: 'Then God'll say, "Hold up—don't let him die. I found a ransom."'
33.25: 'Next thing you know? He fresh again, Lookin' young, feelin' renewed.'
33.26: 'He prays, and God actually listens. He gets joy. God brings him back right.'
33.27: 'And then he says, "Yo, I messed up. I twisted what was right—and it did me no good."'
33.28: 'But God still saved his soul from the grave, Let him live to see the light.'
33.29: 'Look—God do this kind of thing all the time. Twice, even three times if He gotta.'
33.30: 'He do it to pull people back from death, So they can live in the light again.'
33.31: 'So listen, Job—hear what I'm sayin'. Hold tight and let me speak.'
33.32: 'If you got anything to say, I'm ready. I ain't tryna fight you—I wanna see you get right.'
33.33: 'But if you got nothin' else, just sit still. Let me break it down. I'ma teach you real wisdom.'

34.2: 'Y'all wise folks, listen up. You with the knowledge—lean in.'
34.3: 'Just like your tongue knows flavor, Your ears should know truth when you hear it.'
34.4: 'Let's choose what's right together, Let's figure out what's truly good.'
34.5: 'Job said, "I'm righteous, But God done took my justice from me."'
34.6: 'He like, "Why I gotta lie about being innocent? I'm wounded for no reason."'
34.7: 'Who else you know talk like that? Job out here sippin' disrespect like it's water.'
34.8: 'He stay around wicked folks, Walkin' in step with people who do wrong.'
34.9: 'He said, "What's the point of servin' God? Ain't no benefit in it."'
34.10: 'So listen close, y'all with sense: God don't do evil. The Almighty don't play with injustice.'
34.11: 'He pays folks back for what they do. What you sow is what you reap.'
34.12: 'Trust—God never does wrong. The Almighty don't twist justice.'
34.13: 'Who you think put God in charge? Who made Him ruler of the world? Nobody.'
34.14: 'If He took back His Spirit and breath right now—'
34.15: 'All humans would drop dead. Dust. Every last one of us.'
34.16: 'If you got wisdom, listen up. Let this hit your soul:'
34.17: 'You really think somebody who hates justice can run things? You gon' accuse the most righteous One of doin' wrong?'
34.18: 'You wouldn't tell a king, "You worthless," Or call nobles "Wicked" to their face—'
34.19: 'But God don't play favorites, Don't care if you rich or poor—He made all of us the same.'
34.20: 'People die in a flash, in the middle of the night. Mighty folks get snatched up—no warning, no struggle.'
34.21: 'God watches every step we take. Ain't nothin' we do that slips past Him.'
34.22: 'Ain't no dark corner, no deep shadow Where the wicked can hide out.'
34.23: 'God don't need a second opinion Before He makes a move.'
34.24: 'He crushes the powerful without askin' questions, Then raises up somebody else in their spot.'
34.25: 'He knows what they been doin'. He strikes 'em down in the night, and they gone.'
34.26: 'He exposes the wicked in front of everybody— Right out in the open.'
34.27: 'Why? 'Cause they turned their back on Him. They ain't care about His ways.'
34.28: 'And they caused the poor to cry out, And God heard every single tear.'
34.29: 'When God brings peace, who gon' mess that up? But when He hides His face, who can find Him then— Whether it's a nation or just one man?'
34.30: 'He don't let the fake ones rule forever. He know that mess traps people.'
34.31: 'Have you ever heard somebody tell God, "I've been corrected—I'm done wildin'. Show me what I missed, and I won't go back to it"?'
34.32: 'If I messed up, I wanna be taught. If I did wrong, I'll quit for good.'
34.33: 'But should God change His justice just 'cause you ain't feelin' it? You gotta choose for yourself—I ain't here to twist your arm. So if you got somethin' to say, speak up.'
34.34: 'Folks with real sense gon' agree with me— Wise folks who know what's up say this:'
34.35: '"Job talkin' without knowledge. He sound smart, but he missin' the wisdom."'
34.36: 'Man, I wish Job would get the full test— 'Cause the way he answer? Sound like somebody rebelin' against God.'
34.37: 'He stackin' rebellion on top of sin, Clappin' back, gettin' loud, And talkin' way too slick about the Lord.'

35.1: Then Elihu kept goin' and said,
35.2: 'You really think you right for sayin' "My righteousness is more than God's"?'
35.3: 'You said, "What's it do for God if I'm righteous? Ain't no benefit to Him—might as well sin."'
35.4: 'Let me break this down—for you and your boys.'
35.5: 'Look up. Look at the sky. Check out the clouds—they way above you.'
