35.6: 'If you sin, you ain't hurtin' God. Even if you stack sin on sin, He still untouched.'
35.7: 'And if you live righteous, what you givin' God? What He supposed to gain from your good behavior?'
35.8: 'Your wickedness only hits folks like you, And your righteousness? That blesses other people, not God.'
35.9: 'People cry out when they bein' oppressed, They beg for help when power got 'em under pressure.'
35.10: 'But nobody say, "Where's God, the One who made me, The One who gives songs in the middle of the night?"'
35.11: 'He the One who teaches us more than the animals, Gives us more wisdom than birds in the sky.'
35.12: 'But when folks cry out, God don't always answer— 'Cause pride blocks the signal.'
35.13: 'God don't respond to empty noise. The Almighty don't entertain foolishness.'
35.14: 'You said, "I don't see God." But justice is still in front of Him—you just gotta wait on it.'
35.15: 'Now just 'cause He ain't snapped in anger yet, Just 'cause He ain't shut down your foolishness—'
35.16: 'That don't mean you get to talk reckless. But Job? He runnin' his mouth in vain, Pilin' up words with no real knowledge.'

36.2: 'Hold up a lil longer— I got more to say on God's behalf.'
36.3: 'I'm bringin' truth from way off, And I'ma give all credit to my Maker.'
36.4: 'My words ain't fake—trust that. You got someone with real insight talkin' to you now.'
36.5: 'God is powerful—but He don't look down on nobody. His strength come with full understanding.'
36.6: 'He don't keep the wicked alive, But He gives justice to the folks who been done wrong.'
36.7: 'He don't take His eyes off the righteous— He puts 'em on thrones with kings. He sets 'em up and lifts 'em high.'
36.8: 'But if they end up locked up in chains, Caught up in trouble and pain—'
36.9: 'Then God shows 'em what they did wrong, And where they went left.'
36.10: 'He opens their ears to hear Him, And tells them, "Turn back from your mess."'
36.11: 'If they obey and serve Him, They'll live good—prosperous and peaceful.'
36.12: 'But if they ignore Him, They'll die in ignorance, Cut down without even knowin' why.'
36.13: 'Prideful folks keep stackin' up wrath, But they too stubborn to cry out when God's correcting them.'
36.14: 'They die young, And end up lost, livin' among the twisted.'
36.15: 'But the ones who suffer in humility? God delivers them through it. He speaks louder in pain than in peace.'
36.16: 'He was tryin' to pull you out the tight space, Into a wide place full of blessings and freedom. Your table was supposed to be overflowin'.'
36.17: 'But you filled up with the judgment that belongs to the wicked. Now justice caught up to you.'
36.18: 'Be careful—don't let His anger take you out in a flash. You can't pay Him off to dodge the blow.'
36.19: 'Your riches? Your crew? None of that gon' save you when trouble hits.'
36.20: 'Don't be wishin' for the night, When people vanish without warning.'
36.21: 'Watch yourself. Don't turn to sin now— You'd rather sin than suffer, and that's dangerous.'
36.22: 'Look at God—lifted high by His power. Ain't nobody teach like Him.'
36.23: 'Who can tell Him what to do? Who dares to say, "You outta line"?'
36.24: 'Remember to praise His works— Songs been written 'bout how great He is.'
36.25: 'Everybody's seen what He does, Even if they don't fully understand it.'
36.26: 'God is massive—we can't fully know Him. We can't even count His years.'
36.27: 'He pulls up water drop by drop, Turns it into rain through the mist.'
36.28: 'The clouds let it fall, Pourin' out plenty for the earth.'
36.29: 'Can anybody really explain how clouds move? Or how thunder echoes from above?'
36.30: 'He flashes light across the skies, And covers the sea with His presence.'
36.31: 'That same storm? He uses it for judgment— But also to give rain and food in abundance.'
36.32: 'He holds lightning in His hand, And tells it where to strike.'
36.33: 'The thunder speaks loud like a voice, Even the animals know when the storm's comin'.'

37.1: 'Man… just thinkin' about all this makes my heart shake, Feels like it's about to jump out my chest.'
37.2: 'Listen close to the thunder of His voice— That deep rumble that rolls out His mouth.'
37.3: 'He sends that power across the whole sky, His lightning stretches to the ends of the earth.'
37.4: 'Then the roar follows. God speaks through the thunder—loud and majestic. And when He talks, ain't nothin' holdin' it back.'
37.5: 'God's voice got that wonder in it. He does things so big we can't even grasp it.'
37.6: 'He tells the snow to fall, Sends the soft rain and the heavy rain like it's nothin'.'
37.7: 'He shuts down our hustle so we have to pause, So everybody gotta acknowledge His hand.'
37.8: 'Even the animals go hide, Stayin' in their dens till it's safe again.'
37.9: 'Storms come from the south, Cold winds sweep in from the north.'
37.10: 'God's breath brings the ice, Turns open waters into frozen slabs.'
37.11: 'He loads up the clouds with moisture, And sends out bright flashes from inside 'em.'
37.12: 'They swirl and spin under His command, Doin' whatever He says across the whole earth.'
37.13: 'Sometimes it's for correction, Sometimes it's to bless the land, Other times it's just Him showin' mercy.'
37.14: 'Yo Job, stop and think— Look at the amazing things God does.'
37.15: 'Do you know when He sends light from the clouds? Or how He lights up the sky like that?'
37.16: 'Do you understand how clouds float in balance— Those wild works from a God who's flawless in wisdom?'
37.17: 'You ever wonder why it gets hot when the south wind stills the land, And the air just hangs heavy?'
37.18: 'Did you help stretch out the sky, That strong dome like polished metal?'
37.19: 'What would we even say to Him, Job? We too limited to come up with anything in this darkness.'
37.20: 'You really think we gon' tell God we wanna talk? Man, if somebody tried, they'd get swallowed up.'
37.21: 'Shoot—people can't even look directly at the sun When it's bright and clear after the wind passes through.'
37.22: 'God shows up from the north like golden fire. Majesty. Pure awe.'
37.23: 'Look, we can't fully find the Almighty. He too excellent in power. His judgment? Always right. His justice? Full. And He ain't out here tryna hurt people.'
37.24: 'That's why folks fear Him. He don't play favorites, Not even with the "wise."'

38.1: Then the Lord answered Job outta the whirlwind and said,
38.2: 'Who is this messin' up My plans Talkin' loud without knowin' what they sayin'?'
38.3: 'Stand up and take it like a man. I got questions—you gon' answer Me.'
38.4: 'Where were you when I laid down the earth's foundation? Go 'head—explain it if you understand.'
38.5: 'Who decided how wide it should be? You know that too, huh? Who pulled the measuring line across it?'
38.6: 'What's holdin' it all up? Who dropped the cornerstone in place—'
38.7: 'Back when the morning stars were singin', And all heaven's crew was shoutin' for joy?'
38.8: 'Who shut up the sea behind doors When it broke loose like it was bein' born?'
38.9: 'When I wrapped it in clouds like a blanket, And made thick darkness its baby clothes?'
38.10: 'I gave it limits, laid down borders, Set up bars and locked gates.'
38.11: 'And I said, "You can come this far—no further. Your waves stop right here."'
38.12: 'Since you been alive, have you told the morning when to show up? Made the dawn know its place?'
38.13: 'So it could grab the earth by the edges And shake the wicked out like dust from a rug?'
38.14: 'It rolls out like clay under a stamp, And shines like a fresh robe.'
38.15: 'The wicked don't get that light. Their power gets snapped like a twig.'
38.16: 'You ever walk through the ocean floor? Explored the deepest parts of the sea?'
38.17: 'You ever seen the gates of death? Peeked inside the shadow of death's doorway?'
38.18: 'You really understand how wide this earth is? Tell Me, if you know all this.'
38.19: 'Where does the light live? Where darkness post up at?'
38.20: 'You know how to take it to its zone? Lead it back home like GPS?'
38.21: 'You know, right? You was born back then, You been around a long time, huh?'
38.22: 'You ever been inside the snow vault? Or seen where I store the hail—'
38.23: 'The same hail I keep ready for war, For the day trouble comes?'
38.24: 'What's the route light takes? Or the path the east wind travels across the land?'
38.25: 'Who carves out paths for floodwaters? Or directs lightning like it's on a mission?'
38.26: 'Who makes it rain where no one lives? Pourin' down on empty land?'
38.27: 'Just to bring life to dead ground, So grass can grow again?'
38.28: 'Rain got a daddy? Who fathered the drops of dew?'
38.29: 'Who gave birth to the ice? Who delivers heaven's frost?'
38.30: 'Water turns hard like rock, And the deep freezes over like glass.'
38.31: 'Can you lock together the Pleiades stars, Or unbuckle Orion's belt?'
38.32: 'Can you lead out the constellations at the right time, Or guide the Big Dipper and her cubs?'
38.33: 'You know the laws of the universe? Can you make them rule the earth?'
38.34: 'Can you call up the clouds And get rained on just like that?'
38.35: 'Can you send out lightning and have it check in with you like, "Here we are"?'
38.36: 'Who gave humans wisdom? Who put understanding in the mind and heart?'
38.37: 'Who can count the clouds with wisdom? Who tips over the water jars of heaven—'
38.38: 'When the dirt clumps up, And the ground locks up like cement?'
38.39: 'Can you hunt food for the lion, Or feed the young ones when they hungry?'
38.40: 'When they hidin' in the cut, Layin' low waitin' to pounce?'
38.41: 'Who gives the raven its food, When the babies cry out to God, Wanderin' around lookin' for somethin' to eat?'

39.1: 'You know when the wild mountain goats have their babies? Can you mark the moment the deer goes into labor?'
39.2: 'You know how long they carry before birth? You got their due dates on your calendar?'
39.3: 'They crouch down, push through the pain, And bring their babies into the world.'
39.4: 'Those babies grow up strong, eatin' off the land, Then they dip—and they ain't comin' back.'
39.5: 'Who gave the wild donkey its freedom? Who untied the ropes from the wild ass?'
39.6: 'I made the wilderness his crib, The desert his home address.'
39.7: 'He don't care about no city noise, He ain't listenin' to no boss yellin' orders.'
39.8: 'He roams the mountains for food, Lookin' for green wherever he can find it.'
39.9: 'You think the wild ox gon' work for you? Gon' lay down in your barn like a pet?'
39.10: 'Can you tie him up and make him plow your field? You think he gon' follow your lead down in the valley?'
39.11: 'Just 'cause he's strong—you gon' trust him? You really about to leave your grind in his hooves?'
39.12: 'You think he bringin' the harvest back to you, Piling grain on your threshing floor like a worker?'
39.13: 'The ostrich flaps her wings with pride, But they ain't shaped like the stork's.'
39.14: 'She just drops her eggs in the dust, Leaves them out where they could get stepped on.'
39.15: 'She forgets a foot might crush 'em, Or wild animals might come and break 'em.'
39.16: 'She treats her babies like they ain't even hers. She worked for nothin' and don't even care.'
39.17: 'Why? 'Cause I didn't give her wisdom. She ain't got no understanding.'
39.18: 'But when she runs? She lifts off, And clowns the horse and its rider like she runnin' track.'
39.19: 'You the one that gave the horse its strength? You the one who wrapped his neck in thunder?'
39.20: 'You make him jump like a locust, Snortin' so loud it shakes folks up?'
39.21: 'He stompin' the ground, hyped on his power, Rushin' straight into battle without hesitation.'
39.22: 'He laughs at fear—won't flinch, Ain't turnin' around from no sword.'
39.23: 'The quiver rattles, spears and javelins flash, But he's still movin' forward.'
39.24: 'He eats up the ground with his rage, And won't stop even when the trumpet blasts.'
39.25: 'As soon as he hears that trumpet, he like, "Let's go!" He smellin' battle from miles out— He hears the captains shout and knows what time it is.'
39.26: 'Does the hawk fly south 'cause of your wisdom? He spread his wings because you told him to?'
39.27: 'Does the eagle rise up at your command? Make his home way up high?'
39.28: 'He live on the rocks, Builds his spot in the cliffs and strongholds.'
39.29: 'From up there, he watching everything. He peepin' prey from miles away.'
39.30: 'His young ones drink blood like water. And wherever the dead are? That's where he be.'

40.1: Then the Lord kept speakin' to Job and said,
40.2: 'You really tryna check the Almighty? You the one correctin' Me now? If you bold enough to call Me out, go 'head—say somethin'.'
40.3: Then Job answered the Lord and said,
40.4: 'I got nothin'. I'm ashamed. What could I possibly say to You now?'
40.5: 'I already spoke once—I ain't sayin' no more. Said it twice, but I'm done. I'm quiet now.'
40.6: Then the Lord answered Job from the whirlwind and said,
40.7: 'Brace yourself like a man— You gon' answer Me this time.'
40.8: 'You really tryna cancel My judgment Just to make yourself look righteous?'
40.9: 'You got arms like Me? Can you thunder with a voice that shakes the sky?'
40.10: 'Then go ahead—dress yourself in glory. Throw on majesty like it's your outfit.'
40.11: 'Pour out all your anger on the proud. Humble 'em—bring 'em down.'
40.12: 'Take down every arrogant one you see. Make 'em bow right where they stand.'
40.13: 'Bury 'em in the dust. Lock 'em up in the dark where nobody sees 'em.'
40.14: 'If you can do all that, I'll admit you can save yourself.'
40.15: 'Now look at Behemoth—yeah, I made him same time I made you. He eats grass like an ox, but don't get it twisted.'
40.16: 'His strength sittin' heavy in his hips, His power stacked in them core muscles.'
40.17: 'He swings his tail like a cedar tree— His thighs? Built like rope-wrapped steel.'
40.18: 'His bones? Like bronze beams. His ribs? Iron bars.'
40.19: 'He top-tier—firstborn of My creations. Only I got the sword sharp enough for him.'
40.20: 'He chill in the mountains where the wild beasts play, And the hills feed him daily.'
40.21: 'He lays low under the lotus trees, Hidden deep in the marsh and the reeds.'
40.22: 'The trees shade him, And willows hang around him by the stream.'
40.23: 'The river could rage heavy, But he don't flinch. Even if the Jordan floods straight into his face—he cool.'
40.24: 'Try to trap him. Go ahead— Stick a hook in his nose if you bad. But you not. So sit back.'

41.1: 'Can you catch Leviathan with a fish hook? Can you tie his tongue with a string?'
41.2: 'You think you gon' run a rope through his nose, Or stab his jaw with a hook?'
41.3: 'You think he gon' beg you for mercy? Talk sweet to get free?'
41.4: 'You gon' sign a contract with him? Make him your pet for life?'
41.5: 'You tryna play with him like he a pet bird? Put him on a leash for your girls to giggle at?'
41.6: 'You and your homies throwin' a feast off him? Y'all splittin' Leviathan meat at the market?'
41.7: 'You think you can stab through his hide with harpoons, Or crack his skull with a spear?'
41.8: 'Go ahead—touch him. But you better remember that fight, 'Cause you won't want no rematch.'
41.9: 'Ain't no point in even hopin' to beat him— Just lookin' at him makes people freeze.'
41.10: 'Ain't nobody wild enough to challenge him— So tell me: who you think got the guts to stand against Me?'
41.11: 'Who gave Me anything first? Who put Me in debt? Everything under heaven belongs to Me.'
41.12: 'I ain't holdin' back—I'm about to break down this beast: His power, his build, his glory.'
41.13: 'Who can rip off his armor? Who can get close enough to control him?'
41.14: 'You ever looked him in the face? His mouth full of teeth like a nightmare.'
41.15: 'His back is covered in scales so tight, It's like they sealed up with iron.'
41.16: 'Each one locked to the next, Not even air can squeeze between them.'
41.17: 'They so tight they move like one. No separating 'em—solid unity.'
41.18: 'When he sneezes? It's like lightning. His eyes flash like sunrise.'
41.19: 'Fire sparks shoot out his mouth. Burnin' light comin' from deep within.'
41.20: 'Smoke pours from his nose Like a kettle on fire or reeds burnin' up.'
41.21: 'His breath could light a grill. A flame shoot out like a blowtorch.'
41.22: 'His neck drips strength, And just standin' near him brings fear.'
41.23: 'His body's layered up—thick, tight, Ain't nothin' soft about him.'
41.24: 'His heart? Like stone. Hard like a grindstone—cold and unmovable.'
41.25: 'When he rises up, even the brave lose it. They panic when he moves.'
41.26: 'Swing a sword? It bounces off. Spears, arrows, javelins—worthless.'
41.27: 'He treats iron like straw, Bronze like rotten wood.'
41.28: 'Arrows don't faze him. Sling stones? They might as well be dust.'
41.29: 'Darts are like grass to him. Javelins? He laughs at those.'
41.30: 'His belly scrapes the mud like blades. Leaves sharp tracks wherever he walks.'
41.31: 'He makes the ocean bubble like a boiling pot. Turns the sea into somethin' thick like lotion.'
41.32: 'He leaves a trail of white foam so shiny It looks like the sea got silver hair.'
41.33: 'Ain't nobody on earth like him. He was built without fear—none.'
41.34: 'He looks down on everything proud. He the king of the beasts—every creature full of pride answers to him.'

42.1: Then Job replied to the Lord and said,
42.2: 'Lord, I know now—you can do anything. Ain't no plan of Yours that can be stopped.'
42.3: 'You asked me, "Who out here talkin' reckless without knowledge?" That was me. I spoke on things way above my level— Too deep, too wonderful, I just didn't know.'
42.4: 'You told me, "Listen up—I'ma ask the questions, and you gon' answer." So here I am.'
42.5: 'I used to only know about You from what I heard, But now? I see You for myself.'
42.6: 'And I hate how I acted. I repent—sittin' in dust and ashes, humble before You.'
42.7: After the Lord finished speakin' to Job, He turned to Eliphaz the Temanite and said, 'I'm mad at you and your two homeboys. Y'all ain't talk about Me right— But My servant Job did.'
42.8: 'So here's what you do: take seven bulls and seven rams, Go to My servant Job, and offer a burnt offering. And Job gon' pray for y'all. I'll hear him—so I don't treat you like the fools you been actin' like. 'Cause you ain't speak truth about Me like Job did.'
42.9: So Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar went and did what the Lord told 'em, And the Lord accepted Job's prayer.
42.10: And when Job prayed for his friends, The Lord flipped the script and restored everything he lost— In fact, He doubled it.
42.11: Then all his people—his brothers, sisters, and old friends— Pulled up and had a meal with him at his house. They comforted him for all the pain the Lord had allowed. And each one brought him some silver and a gold ring.
42.12: God blessed Job's latter days even more than his beginning. He ended up with 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, And 1,000 female donkeys.
42.13: He had seven sons and three daughters again.
42.14: He named the first daughter Jemimah, The second Keziah, And the third Keren-Happuch.
42.15: And across the whole land, There wasn't a woman alive as fine as Job's daughters. And he gave them an inheritance right along with their brothers.
42.16: After all this, Job lived another 140 years. He saw his kids, grandkids, great-grands—four generations deep.
42.17: Then Job passed away, Old, full of years, full of life, full of peace.
